rules.body: Apply when deferred edits belong to a persistent document owner while the current view owns only its subscription. Keep each document's trailing task in the coordinator dictionary and associate its consumer with that document ID. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "Document buffers are owned by the coordinator dictionary, while Badge owns only a live subscription."

Send edits through the existing document trailing task: replace pending text and restart the 120 ms quiet interval on each edit; consume only the latest pending text. Keep the task reusable after consumption. Evidence: TASK: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/services.js: "push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); },"

Preserve pending document persistence when navigation, close, or disposal retires the view: flush the departing document buffer before departure returns, rather than canceling it as subscription cleanup. Evidence: TASK: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." README.md: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge." src/coordinator.js: "close(){++request;retire();},dispose(){api.close();}"

Treat a flush as a synchronous reentry boundary. Capture the departing view, detach it from current state, stop its subscription, and finish clearing its rendering before flushing its buffer. After the flush, an interrupted open must recheck its request identity before publishing its destination; retirement must not clear a view installed by the save callback. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." src/coordinator.js: "const mine=++request;retire();if(true&&mine!==request)return;"

Clear the consumed pending value and timer before invoking the save consumer, so a synchronous callback does not encounter the same pending save again and later pushes remain usable. Preserve empty document text as a valid value. Evidence: src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

Preserve document identity, text, status payloads, rendering, subscription cleanup, and the existing public methods. Keep the adjacent preview's separate 40 ms trailing task and cancel-on-hide behavior. Evidence: docs/host-api.md: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." TASK: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));\n  return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Verify with controlled timers that a burst writes nothing before its quiet boundary, writes its latest text at that boundary, and allows a subsequent burst. Verify navigation, close, and disposal with pending text, including empty text, and advance timers afterward to detect duplicate saves. During a departure flush, synchronously navigate or close from a store listener and check that the callback's chosen state remains authoritative. These checks exercise TASK: "Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." and docs/host-api.md: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously."

limitations: Applies to persistent document buffers with synchronous store-listener navigation; it does not establish a general policy for transient tasks or arbitrary host-callback reentry.
The task and public sources do not specify recovery when store, timer, subscription, or rendering callbacks throw.
Attempt 1 supplies one successful implementation example. Its reported results do not prove causality, exhaustive correctness, or benefit on other tasks.
The static review hint identifies a review question, not a proven defect. Evaluation observations and the automatic contract are not normative requirements.
